40:27.ar: وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّي عُذۡتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُم مِّن كُلِّ مُتَكَبِّرࣲ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُ بِيَوۡمِ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
40:27.en: Moses said: Lo! I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every scorner who believeth not in a Day of Reckoning

40:28.ar: وَقَالَ رَجُلࣱ مُّؤۡمِنࣱ مِّنۡ ءَالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ يَكۡتُمُ إِيمَٰنَهُۥٓ أَتَقۡتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّيَ ٱللَّهُ وَقَدۡ جَآءَكُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ مِن رَّبِّكُمۡۖ وَإِن يَكُ كَٰذِبࣰ ا فَعَلَيۡهِ كَذِبُهُۥۖ وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقࣰ ا يُصِبۡكُم بَعۡضُ ٱلَّذِي يَعِدُكُمۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي مَنۡ هُوَ مُسۡرِفࣱ كَذَّابࣱ‏
40:28.en: And a believing man of Pharaoh's family, who hid his faith, said: Would ye kill a man because he saith: My Lord is Allah, and hath brought you clear proofs from your Lord? If he is lying, then his lie is upon him; and if he is truthful, then some of that wherewith he threateneth you will strike you. Lo! Allah guideth not one who is a prodigal, a liar

40:29.ar: يَٰقَوۡمِ لَكُمُ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ ظَٰهِرِينَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَمَن يَنصُرُنَا مِنۢ بَأۡسِ ٱللَّهِ إِن جَآءَنَاۚ قَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ مَآ أُرِيكُمۡ إِلَّا مَآ أَرَىٰ وَمَآ أَهۡدِيكُمۡ إِلَّا سَبِيلَ ٱلرَّشَادِ
40:29.en: O my people! Yours is the kingdom to-day, ye being uppermost in the land. But who would save us from the wrath of Allah should it reach us? Pharaoh said: I do but show you what I think, and I do but guide you to wise policy

40:30.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَامَنَ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيۡكُم مِّثۡلَ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابِ
40:30.en: And he who believed said: O my people! Lo! I fear for you a fate like that of the factions (of old)

40:31.ar: مِثۡلَ دَأۡبِ قَوۡمِ نُوحࣲ وَعَادࣲ وَثَمُودَ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡۚ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ يُرِيدُ ظُلۡمࣰ ا لِّلۡعِبَادِ
40:31.en: A plight like that of Noah's folk, and A'ad and Thamud, and those after them, and Allah willeth no injustice for (His) slaves

40:32.ar: وَيَٰقَوۡمِ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلتَّنَادِ
40:32.en: And, O my people! Lo! I fear for you a Day of Summoning

40:33.ar: يَوۡمَ تُوَلُّونَ مُدۡبِرِينَ مَا لَكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۡ عَاصِمࣲۗ وَمَن يُضۡلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنۡ هَادࣲ‏
40:33.en: A day when ye will turn to flee, having no preserver from Allah: and he whom Allah sendeth astray, for him there is no guide

40:34.ar: وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَكُمۡ يُوسُفُ مِن قَبۡلُ بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ فَمَا زِلۡتُمۡ فِي شَكࣲّ مِّمَّا جَآءَكُم بِهِۦۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا هَلَكَ قُلۡتُمۡ لَن يَبۡعَثَ ٱللَّهُ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ رَسُولࣰ اۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَنۡ هُوَ مُسۡرِفࣱ مُّرۡتَابٌ
40:34.en: And verily Joseph brought you of old clear proofs, yet ye ceased not to be in doubt concerning what he brought you till, when he died, ye said: Allah will not send any messenger after him. Thus Allah deceiveth him who is a prodigal, a doubter

40:35.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُجَٰدِلُونَ فِيٓ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ سُلۡطَٰنٍ أَتَىٰهُمۡۖ كَبُرَ مَقۡتًا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَعِندَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَطۡبَعُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ قَلۡبِ مُتَكَبِّرࣲ جَبَّارࣲ‏
40:35.en: Those who wrangle concerning the revelations of Allah without any warrant that hath come unto them, it is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe. Thus doth Allah print on every arrogant, disdainful heart

40:36.ar: وَقَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ يَٰهَٰمَٰنُ ٱبۡنِ لِي صَرۡحࣰ ا لَّعَلِّيٓ أَبۡلُغُ ٱلۡأَسۡبَٰبَ
40:36.en: And Pharaoh said: O Haman! Build for me a tower that haply I may reach the roads

40:37.ar: أَسۡبَٰبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ فَأَطَّلِعَ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُۥ كَٰذِبࣰ اۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِفِرۡعَوۡنَ سُوٓءُ عَمَلِهِۦ وَصُدَّ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِۚ وَمَا كَيۡدُ فِرۡعَوۡنَ إِلَّا فِي تَبَابࣲ‏
40:37.en: The roads of the heavens, and may look upon the god of Moses, though verily I think him a liar. Thus was the evil that he did made fairseeming unto Pharaoh, and he was debarred from the (right) way. The plot of Pharaoh ended but in ruin

40:38.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَامَنَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱتَّبِعُونِ أَهۡدِكُمۡ سَبِيلَ ٱلرَّشَادِ
40:38.en: And he who believed said: O my people! Follow me. I will show you the way of right conduct

40:39.ar: يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنَّمَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا مَتَٰعࣱ وَإِنَّ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ هِيَ دَارُ ٱلۡقَرَارِ
40:39.en: O my people! Lo! this life of the world is but a passing comfort, and lo! the Hereafter, that is the enduring home

40:40.ar: مَنۡ عَمِلَ سَيِّئَةࣰ فَلَا يُجۡزَىٰٓ إِلَّا مِثۡلَهَاۖ وَمَنۡ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنࣱ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يَدۡخُلُونَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ يُرۡزَقُونَ فِيهَا بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابࣲ‏
40:40.en: Whoso doeth an ill-deed, he will be repaid the like thereof, while whoso doeth right, whether male or female, and is a believer, (all) such will enter the Garden, where they will be nourished without stint

40:41.ar: ۞وَيَٰقَوۡمِ مَا لِيٓ أَدۡعُوكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلنَّجَوٰةِ وَتَدۡعُونَنِيٓ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ
40:41.en: And, O my people! What aileth me that I call you unto deliverance when ye call me unto the Fire

40:42.ar: تَدۡعُونَنِي لِأَكۡفُرَ بِٱللَّهِ وَأُشۡرِكَ بِهِۦ مَا لَيۡسَ لِي بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ وَأَنَا۠ أَدۡعُوكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡغَفَّٰرِ
40:42.en: Ye call me to disbelieve in Allah and ascribe unto Him as partners that whereof I have no knowledge, while I call you unto the Mighty, the Forgiver

40:43.ar: لَا جَرَمَ أَنَّمَا تَدۡعُونَنِيٓ إِلَيۡهِ لَيۡسَ لَهُۥ دَعۡوَةࣱ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَلَا فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ وَأَنَّ مَرَدَّنَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأَنَّ ٱلۡمُسۡرِفِينَ هُمۡ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ
40:43.en: Assuredly that whereunto ye call me hath no claim in the world or in the Hereafter, and our return will be unto Allah, and the prodigals will be owners of the Fire

40:44.ar: فَسَتَذۡكُرُونَ مَآ أَقُولُ لَكُمۡۚ وَأُفَوِّضُ أَمۡرِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَصِيرُۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ
40:44.en: And ye will remember what I say unto you. I confide my cause unto Allah. Lo! Allah is Seer of (His) slaves

40:45.ar: فَوَقَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِ مَا مَكَرُواْۖ وَحَاقَ بِـَٔالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ سُوٓءُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
40:45.en: So Allah warded off from him the evils which they plotted, while a dreadful doom encompassed Pharaoh's folk

40:46.ar: ٱلنَّارُ يُعۡرَضُونَ عَلَيۡهَا غُدُوࣰّ ا وَعَشِيࣰّ اۚ وَيَوۡمَ تَقُومُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدۡخِلُوٓاْ ءَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ أَشَدَّ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
40:46.en: The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening; and on the day when the Hour upriseth (it is said): Cause Pharaoh's folk to enter the most awful doom

40:47.ar: وَإِذۡ يَتَحَآجُّونَ فِي ٱلنَّارِ فَيَقُولُ ٱلضُّعَفَٰٓؤُاْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُوٓاْ إِنَّا كُنَّا لَكُمۡ تَبَعࣰ ا فَهَلۡ أَنتُم مُّغۡنُونَ عَنَّا نَصِيبࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ
40:47.en: And when they wrangle in the Fire, the weak say unto those who were proud: Lo! we were a following unto you; will ye therefor rid us of a portion of the Fire

40:48.ar: قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُوٓاْ إِنَّا كُلࣱّ فِيهَآ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدۡ حَكَمَ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡعِبَادِ
40:48.en: Those who were proud say: Lo! we are all (together) herein. Lo! Allah hath judged between (His) slaves

40:49.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِي ٱلنَّارِ لِخَزَنَةِ جَهَنَّمَ ٱدۡعُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ يُخَفِّفۡ عَنَّا يَوۡمࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
40:49.en: And those in the Fire say unto the guards of hell: Entreat your Lord that He relieve us of a day of the torment

40:50.ar: قَالُوٓاْ أَوَلَمۡ تَكُ تَأۡتِيكُمۡ رُسُلُكُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰۚ قَالُواْ فَٱدۡعُواْۗ وَمَا دُعَٰٓؤُاْ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَٰلٍ
40:50.en: They say: Came not your messengers unto you with clear proofs? They say: Yea, verily. They say: Then do ye pray, although the prayer of disbelievers is in vain

40:51.ar: إِنَّا لَنَنصُرُ رُسُلَنَا وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَيَوۡمَ يَقُومُ ٱلۡأَشۡهَٰدُ
40:51.en: Lo! We verily do help Our messengers, and those who believe, in the life of the world and on the day when the witnesses arise

40:52.ar: يَوۡمَ لَا يَنفَعُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ مَعۡذِرَتُهُمۡۖ وَلَهُمُ ٱللَّعۡنَةُ وَلَهُمۡ سُوٓءُ ٱلدَّارِ
40:52.en: The day when their excuse availeth not the evil-doers, and theirs is the curse, and theirs the ill abode

40:53.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَأَوۡرَثۡنَا بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ
40:53.en: And We verily gave Moses the guidance, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture

40:54.en: A guide and a reminder for men of understanding

40:55.ar: فَٱصۡبِرۡ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لِذَنۢبِكَ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلۡعَشِيِّ وَٱلۡإِبۡكَٰرِ
40:55.en: Then have patience (O Muhammad). Lo! the promise of Allah is true. And ask forgiveness of thy sin, and hymn the praise of thy Lord at fall of night and in the early hours

40:56.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُجَٰدِلُونَ فِيٓ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ سُلۡطَٰنٍ أَتَىٰهُمۡ إِن فِي صُدُورِهِمۡ إِلَّا كِبۡرࣱ مَّا هُم بِبَٰلِغِيهِۚ فَٱسۡتَعِذۡ بِٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡبَصِيرُ
40:56.en: Lo! those who wrangle concerning the revelations of Allah without a warrant having come unto them, there is naught else in their breasts save pride which they will never attain. So take thou refuge in Allah. Lo! He, only He, is the Hearer, the Seer

40:57.ar: لَخَلۡقُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَكۡبَرُ مِنۡ خَلۡقِ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
40:57.en: Assuredly the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind; but most of mankind know not

40:58.ar: وَمَا يَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡأَعۡمَىٰ وَٱلۡبَصِيرُ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَلَا ٱلۡمُسِيٓءُۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تَتَذَكَّرُونَ
40:58.en: And the blind man and the seer are not equal, neither are those who believe and do good works (equal with) the evil-doer. Little do ye reflect

40:59.ar: إِنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ لَأٓتِيَةࣱ لَّا رَيۡبَ فِيهَا وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
40:59.en: Lo! the Hour is surely coming, there is no doubt thereof; yet most of mankind believe not

40:60.ar: وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ٱدۡعُونِيٓ أَسۡتَجِبۡ لَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ عَنۡ عِبَادَتِي سَيَدۡخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ
40:60.en: And your Lord hath said: Pray unto Me and I will hear your prayer. Lo! those who scorn My service, they will enter hell, disgraced

40:61.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ لِتَسۡكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَٱلنَّهَارَ مُبۡصِرًاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَشۡكُرُونَ
40:61.en: Allah it is Who hath appointed for you night that ye may rest therein, and day for seeing. Lo! Allah is a Lord of bounty for mankind, yet most of mankind give not thanks

41:2.en: A revelation from the Beneficent, the Merciful

41:3.ar: كِتَٰبࣱ فُصِّلَتۡ ءَايَٰتُهُۥ قُرۡءَانًا عَرَبِيࣰّ ا لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡلَمُونَ
41:3.en: A Scripture whereof the verses are expounded, a Lecture in Arabic for people who have knowledge

41:4.ar: بَشِيرࣰ ا وَنَذِيرࣰ ا فَأَعۡرَضَ أَكۡثَرُهُمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يَسۡمَعُونَ
41:4.en: Good tidings and a warning. But most of them turn away so that they hear not

41:5.ar: وَقَالُواْ قُلُوبُنَا فِيٓ أَكِنَّةࣲ مِّمَّا تَدۡعُونَآ إِلَيۡهِ وَفِيٓ ءَاذَانِنَا وَقۡرࣱ وَمِنۢ بَيۡنِنَا وَبَيۡنِكَ حِجَابࣱ فَٱعۡمَلۡ إِنَّنَا عَٰمِلُونَ
41:5.en: And they say: Our hearts are protected from that unto which thou (O Muhammad) callest us, and in our ears there is a deafness, and between us and thee there is a veil. Act, then. Lo! we also shall be acting

41:6.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ بَشَرࣱ مِّثۡلُكُمۡ يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمۡ إِلَٰهࣱ وَٰحِدࣱ فَٱسۡتَقِيمُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرُوهُۗ وَوَيۡلࣱ لِّلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
41:6.en: Say (unto them O Muhammad): I am only a mortal like you. It is inspired in me that your Allah is One Allah, therefor take the straight path unto Him and seek forgiveness of Him. And woe unto the idolaters

41:7.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَهُم بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمۡ كَٰفِرُونَ
41:7.en: Who give not the poor-due, and who are disbelievers in the Hereafter

41:8.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَهُمۡ أَجۡرٌ غَيۡرُ مَمۡنُونࣲ‏
41:8.en: Lo! as for those who believe and do good works, for them is a reward enduring

41:9.ar: ۞قُلۡ أَئِنَّكُمۡ لَتَكۡفُرُونَ بِٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِي يَوۡمَيۡنِ وَتَجۡعَلُونَ لَهُۥٓ أَندَادࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
41:9.en: Say (O Muhammad, unto the idolaters): Disbelieve ye verily in Him Who created the earth in two Days, and ascribe ye unto Him rivals? He (and none else) is the Lord of the Worlds

41:10.ar: وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَٰسِيَ مِن فَوۡقِهَا وَبَٰرَكَ فِيهَا وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَآ أَقۡوَٰتَهَا فِيٓ أَرۡبَعَةِ أَيَّامࣲ سَوَآءࣰ لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ
41:10.en: He placed therein firm hills rising above it, and blessed it and measured therein its sustenance in four Days, alike for (all) who ask

41:11.ar: ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانࣱ فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلۡأَرۡضِ ٱئۡتِيَا طَوۡعًا أَوۡ كَرۡهࣰ ا قَالَتَآ أَتَيۡنَا طَآئِعِينَ
41:11.en: Then turned He to the heaven when it was smoke, and said unto it and unto the earth: Come both of you, willingly or loth. They said: We come, obedient

41:12.ar: فَقَضَىٰهُنَّ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَاتࣲ فِي يَوۡمَيۡنِ وَأَوۡحَىٰ فِي كُلِّ سَمَآءٍ أَمۡرَهَاۚ وَزَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا بِمَصَٰبِيحَ وَحِفۡظࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَقۡدِيرُ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡعَلِيمِ
41:12.en: Then He ordained them seven heavens in two Days and inspired in each heaven its mandate; and We decked the nether heaven with lamps, and rendered it inviolable. That is the measuring of the Mighty, the Knower

41:13.ar: فَإِنۡ أَعۡرَضُواْ فَقُلۡ أَنذَرۡتُكُمۡ صَٰعِقَةࣰ مِّثۡلَ صَٰعِقَةِ عَادࣲ وَثَمُودَ
41:13.en: But if they turn away, then say: I warn you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt (which fell of old upon the tribes) of A'ad and Thamud

41:14.ar: إِذۡ جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلرُّسُلُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَۖ قَالُواْ لَوۡ شَآءَ رَبُّنَا لَأَنزَلَ مَلَٰٓئِكَةࣰ فَإِنَّا بِمَآ أُرۡسِلۡتُم بِهِۦ كَٰفِرُونَ
41:14.en: When their messengers came unto them from before them and behind them, saying: Worship none but Allah! they said: If our Lord had willed, He surely would have sent down angels (unto us), so lo! we are disbelievers in that wherewith ye have been sent

41:15.ar: فَأَمَّا عَادࣱ فَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَقَالُواْ مَنۡ أَشَدُّ مِنَّا قُوَّةًۖ أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَهُمۡ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنۡهُمۡ قُوَّةࣰۖ وَكَانُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يَجۡحَدُونَ
41:15.en: As for A'ad, they were arrogant in the land without right, and they said: Who is mightier than us in power? Could they not see that Allah Who created them, He was mightier than them in power? And they denied Our revelations

41:16.ar: فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ رِيحࣰ ا صَرۡصَرࣰ ا فِيٓ أَيَّامࣲ نَّحِسَاتࣲ لِّنُذِيقَهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡخِزۡيِ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ أَخۡزَىٰۖ وَهُمۡ لَا يُنصَرُونَ
41:16.en: Therefor We let loose on them a raging wind in evil days, that We might make them taste the torment of disgrace in the life of the world. And verily the doom of the Hereafter will be more shameful, and they will not be helped

41:17.ar: وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيۡنَٰهُمۡ فَٱسۡتَحَبُّواْ ٱلۡعَمَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡهُدَىٰ فَأَخَذَتۡهُمۡ صَٰعِقَةُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡهُونِ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ
41:17.en: And as for Thamud, We gave them guidance, but they preferred blindness to the guidance, so the bolt of the doom of humiliation overtook them because of what they used to earn

41:18.en: And We delivered those who believed and used to keep their duty to Allah

41:19.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يُحۡشَرُ أَعۡدَآءُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ فَهُمۡ يُوزَعُونَ
41:19.en: And (make mention of) the day when the enemies of Allah are gathered unto the Fire, they are driven on

41:20.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا مَا جَآءُوهَا شَهِدَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ سَمۡعُهُمۡ وَأَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ وَجُلُودُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
41:20.en: Till, when they reach it, their ears and their eyes and their skins testify against them as to what they used to do

41:21.ar: وَقَالُواْ لِجُلُودِهِمۡ لِمَ شَهِدتُّمۡ عَلَيۡنَاۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَنطَقَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنطَقَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۚ وَهُوَ خَلَقَكُمۡ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
41:21.en: And they say unto their skins: Why testify ye against us? They say: Allah hath given us speech Who giveth speech to all things, and Who created you at the first, and unto Whom ye are returned

41:22.ar: وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَسۡتَتِرُونَ أَن يَشۡهَدَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ سَمۡعُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَبۡصَٰرُكُمۡ وَلَا جُلُودُكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن ظَنَنتُمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَعۡلَمُ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
41:22.en: Ye did not hide yourselves lest your ears and your eyes and your skins should testify against you, but ye deemed that Allah knew not much of what ye did

41:23.ar: وَذَٰلِكُمۡ ظَنُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي ظَنَنتُم بِرَبِّكُمۡ أَرۡدَىٰكُمۡ فَأَصۡبَحۡتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
41:23.en: That, your thought which ye did think about your Lord, hath ruined you; and ye find yourselves (this day) among the lost

41:24.ar: فَإِن يَصۡبِرُواْ فَٱلنَّارُ مَثۡوࣰ ى لَّهُمۡۖ وَإِن يَسۡتَعۡتِبُواْ فَمَا هُم مِّنَ ٱلۡمُعۡتَبِينَ
41:24.en: And though they are resigned, yet the Fire is still their home; and if they ask for favour, yet they are not of those unto whom favour can be shown

39:68.ar: وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَصَعِقَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُۖ ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيهِ أُخۡرَىٰ فَإِذَا هُمۡ قِيَامࣱ يَنظُرُونَ
39:68.en: And the trumpet is blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are in the earth swoon away, save him whom Allah willeth. Then it is blown a second time, and behold them standing waiting

39:69.ar: وَأَشۡرَقَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّهَا وَوُضِعَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ وَجِاْيٓءَ بِٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَٱلشُّهَدَآءِ وَقُضِيَ بَيۡنَهُم بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
39:69.en: And the earth shineth with the light of her Lord, and the Book is set up, and the prophets and the witnesses are brought, and it is judged between them with truth, and they are not wronged

39:70.ar: وَوُفِّيَتۡ كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ مَّا عَمِلَتۡ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا يَفۡعَلُونَ
39:70.en: And each soul is paid in full for what it did. And He is Best Aware of what they do

39:71.ar: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ زُمَرًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا فُتِحَتۡ أَبۡوَٰبُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَآ أَلَمۡ يَأۡتِكُمۡ رُسُلࣱ مِّنكُمۡ يَتۡلُونَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّكُمۡ وَيُنذِرُونَكُمۡ لِقَآءَ يَوۡمِكُمۡ هَٰذَاۚ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِنۡ حَقَّتۡ كَلِمَةُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
39:71.en: And those who disbelieve are driven unto hell in troops till, when they reach it and the gates thereof are opened, and the warders thereof say unto them: Came there not unto you messengers of your own, reciting unto you the revelations of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day? they say: Yea, verily. But the word of doom of disbelievers is fulfilled

39:72.ar: قِيلَ ٱدۡخُلُوٓاْ أَبۡوَٰبَ جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۖ فَبِئۡسَ مَثۡوَى ٱلۡمُتَكَبِّرِينَ
39:72.en: It is said (unto them): Enter ye the gates of hell to dwell therein. Thus hapless is the journey's end of the scorners

39:73.ar: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْ رَبَّهُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡجَنَّةِ زُمَرًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتۡ أَبۡوَٰبُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَا سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡ طِبۡتُمۡ فَٱدۡخُلُوهَا خَٰلِدِينَ
39:73.en: And those who keep their duty to their Lord are driven unto the Garden in troops till, when they reach it, and the gates thereof are opened, and the warders thereof say unto them: Peace be unto you! Ye are good, so enter ye (the Garden of delight), to dwell therein

39:74.ar: وَقَالُواْ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي صَدَقَنَا وَعۡدَهُۥ وَأَوۡرَثَنَا ٱلۡأَرۡضَ نَتَبَوَّأُ مِنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ حَيۡثُ نَشَآءُۖ فَنِعۡمَ أَجۡرُ ٱلۡعَٰمِلِينَ
39:74.en: They say: Praise be to Allah, Who hath fulfilled His promise unto us and hath made us inherit the land, sojourning in the Garden where we will! So bounteous is the wage of workers

39:75.ar: وَتَرَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ حَآفِّينَ مِنۡ حَوۡلِ ٱلۡعَرۡشِ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّهِمۡۚ وَقُضِيَ بَيۡنَهُم بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ وَقِيلَ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
39:75.en: And thou (O Muhammad) seest the angels thronging round the Throne, hymning the praises of their Lord. And they are judged aright. And it is said: Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

40:62.ar: ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمۡ خَٰلِقُ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُؤۡفَكُونَ
40:62.en: Such is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things, There is no Allah save Him. How then are ye perverted

40:63.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ يُؤۡفَكُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَانُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ يَجۡحَدُونَ
40:63.en: Thus are they perverted who deny the revelations of Allah

40:64.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ قَرَارࣰ ا وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءࣰ وَصَوَّرَكُمۡ فَأَحۡسَنَ صُوَرَكُمۡ وَرَزَقَكُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِۚ ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمۡۖ فَتَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
40:64.en: Allah it is Who appointed for you the earth for a dwelling-place and the sky for a canopy, and fashioned you and perfected your shapes, and hath provided you with good things. Such is Allah, your Lord. Then blessed be Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

40:65.ar: هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَٱدۡعُوهُ مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَۗ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
40:65.en: He is the Living One. There is no Allah save Him. So pray unto Him, making religion pure for Him (only). Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

40:67.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن تُرَابࣲ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطۡفَةࣲ ثُمَّ مِنۡ عَلَقَةࣲ ثُمَّ يُخۡرِجُكُمۡ طِفۡلࣰ ا ثُمَّ لِتَبۡلُغُوٓاْ أَشُدَّكُمۡ ثُمَّ لِتَكُونُواْ شُيُوخࣰ اۚ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُتَوَفَّىٰ مِن قَبۡلُۖ وَلِتَبۡلُغُوٓاْ أَجَلࣰ ا مُّسَمࣰّ ى وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
40:67.en: He it is Who created you from dust, then from a drop (of seed) then from a clot, then bringeth you forth as a child, then (ordaineth) that ye attain full strength and afterward that ye become old men - though some among you die before - and that ye reach an appointed term, that haply ye may understand

40:68.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُۖ فَإِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
40:68.en: He it is Who quickeneth and giveth death. When He ordaineth a thing, He saith unto it only: Be! and it is

40:69.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُجَٰدِلُونَ فِيٓ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ أَنَّىٰ يُصۡرَفُونَ
40:69.en: Hast thou not seen those who wrangle concerning the revelations of Allah, how they are turned away

40:70.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَبِمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا بِهِۦ رُسُلَنَاۖ فَسَوۡفَ يَعۡلَمُونَ
40:70.en: Those who deny the Scripture and that wherewith We send Our messengers. But they will come to know

40:71.ar: إِذِ ٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلُ فِيٓ أَعۡنَٰقِهِمۡ وَٱلسَّلَٰسِلُ يُسۡحَبُونَ
40:71.en: When carcans are about their necks and chains. They are dragged

40:72.ar: فِي ٱلۡحَمِيمِ ثُمَّ فِي ٱلنَّارِ يُسۡجَرُونَ
40:72.en: Through boiling waters; then they are thrust into the Fire

40:73.ar: ثُمَّ قِيلَ لَهُمۡ أَيۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡ تُشۡرِكُونَ
40:73.en: Then it is said unto them: Where are (all) that ye used to make partners (in the Sovereignty)

40:74.ar: مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۖ قَالُواْ ضَلُّواْ عَنَّا بَل لَّمۡ نَكُن نَّدۡعُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
40:74.en: Beside Allah? They say: They have failed us; but we used not to pray to anything before. Thus doth Allah send astray the disbelievers (in His guidance)

40:75.ar: ذَٰلِكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَفۡرَحُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَبِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَمۡرَحُونَ
40:75.en: (And it is said unto them): This is because ye exulted in the earth without right, and because ye were petulant

40:76.ar: ٱدۡخُلُوٓاْ أَبۡوَٰبَ جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۖ فَبِئۡسَ مَثۡوَى ٱلۡمُتَكَبِّرِينَ
40:76.en: Enter ye the gates of hell, to dwell therein. Evil is the habitation of the scornful

40:77.ar: فَٱصۡبِرۡ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّۚ فَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعۡضَ ٱلَّذِي نَعِدُهُمۡ أَوۡ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِلَيۡنَا يُرۡجَعُونَ
40:77.en: Then have patience (O Muhammad). Lo! the promise of Allah is true. And whether we let thee see a part of that which We promise them, or (whether) We cause thee to die, still unto Us they will be brought back

40:78.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا رُسُلࣰ ا مِّن قَبۡلِكَ مِنۡهُم مَّن قَصَصۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ وَمِنۡهُم مَّن لَّمۡ نَقۡصُصۡ عَلَيۡكَۗ وَمَا كَانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَن يَأۡتِيَ بِـَٔايَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۚ فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ قُضِيَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَخَسِرَ هُنَالِكَ ٱلۡمُبۡطِلُونَ
40:78.en: Verily We sent messengers before thee, among them those of whom We have told thee, and some of whom We have not told thee; and it was not given to any messenger that he should bring a portent save by Allah's leave, but when Allah's commandment cometh (the cause) is judged aright, and the followers of vanity will then be lost

40:79.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمَ لِتَرۡكَبُواْ مِنۡهَا وَمِنۡهَا تَأۡكُلُونَ
40:79.en: Allah it is Who hath appointed for you cattle, that ye may ride on some of them, and eat of some

40:80.ar: وَلَكُمۡ فِيهَا مَنَٰفِعُ وَلِتَبۡلُغُواْ عَلَيۡهَا حَاجَةࣰ فِي صُدُورِكُمۡ وَعَلَيۡهَا وَعَلَى ٱلۡفُلۡكِ تُحۡمَلُونَ
40:80.en: (Many) benefits ye have from them - and that ye may satisfy by their means a need that is in your breasts, and may be borne upon them as upon the ship

40:81.ar: وَيُرِيكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ فَأَيَّ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ تُنكِرُونَ
40:81.en: And He showeth you His tokens. Which, then, of the tokens of Allah do ye deny

40:82.ar: أَفَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَيَنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۚ كَانُوٓاْ أَكۡثَرَ مِنۡهُمۡ وَأَشَدَّ قُوَّةࣰ وَءَاثَارࣰ ا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَمَآ أَغۡنَىٰ عَنۡهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ
40:82.en: Have they not travelled in the land to see the nature of the consequence for those before them? They were more numerous than these, and mightier in power and (in the) traces (which they left behind them) in the earth. But all that they used to earn availed them not

40:83.ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَتۡهُمۡ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ فَرِحُواْ بِمَا عِندَهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ وَحَاقَ بِهِم مَّا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
40:83.en: And when their messengers brought them clear proofs (of Allah's Sovereignty) they exulted in the knowledge they (themselves) possessed. And that which they were wont to mock befell them

40:84.ar: فَلَمَّا رَأَوۡاْ بَأۡسَنَا قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَحۡدَهُۥ وَكَفَرۡنَا بِمَا كُنَّا بِهِۦ مُشۡرِكِينَ
40:84.en: Then, when they saw Our doom, they said: We believe in Allah only and reject (all) that we used to associate (with Him)

40:85.ar: فَلَمۡ يَكُ يَنفَعُهُمۡ إِيمَٰنُهُمۡ لَمَّا رَأَوۡاْ بَأۡسَنَاۖ سُنَّتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِي قَدۡ خَلَتۡ فِي عِبَادِهِۦۖ وَخَسِرَ هُنَالِكَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ
40:85.en: But their faith could not avail them when they saw Our doom. This is Allah's law which hath ever taken course for His bondmen. And then the disbelievers will be ruined

oFd5KSd3Xnc.speaker: adnan
oFd5KSd3Xnc.speaker_note: his A Juz A Day series; welcomes viewers and teaches throughout in his own voice
oFd5KSd3Xnc.title: A Juz A Day: 24th Juz - Sincere Devotion to Allah
oFd5KSd3Xnc.one_line: Az-Zumar, Ghafir and the opening of Fussilat: sincere devotion to Allah alone, hope in His mercy, and patient dawah whatever the results.
oFd5KSd3Xnc.summary: He covers the 24th juz, starting from the beginning of Surah Az-Zumar for continuity, and frames the surah around sincere devotion to Allah. He dismantles the idea that people need intermediaries to reach Allah: the One who created, provides and shapes us in the womb needs no go-between, and His names Al-Wahid and Al-Qahhar come together so His oneness is never mistaken for weakness. He contrasts the fickle person who calls on Allah only in hardship with the one who worships through the night, explains that real knowledge changes behaviour, and teaches that patience is a state whose reward keeps counting. The parable of the slave with quarrelling masters shows why worshipping many gods leaves no devotion at all. The closing scenes of Az-Zumar, groups led to hell and to paradise, stress that no one enters the fire without the message having reached them. He then introduces the seven Ha Meem surahs and their shared themes, and dwells on Ghafir: the angels praying for believers, and the believing man from Pharaoh's household who argued for Musa from a position of power. The lesson for Muslims in North America is to live and convey Islam with sincerity and patience, leave the results to Allah, and expect help from unexpected places.

outline.heading: The 24th juz and the theme of Az-Zumar
outline.gist: He maps the juz across Az-Zumar, Ghafir and Fussilat, notes that the Ha Meem surahs begin here, and names sincere devotion as the core message of Az-Zumar.

outline.heading: Worship Allah sincerely, without intermediaries
outline.gist: The polytheists admitted their idols were not the Creator and claimed they only brought them closer to Allah; he calls this a detour around the obvious question.

outline.heading: Allah has no offspring and runs an ordered creation
outline.gist: A son would be the ultimate intermediary, yet Allah is above that; He created the heavens and the earth with purpose and set the sun and moon in motion.

outline.heading: Why Al-Wahid comes paired with Al-Qahhar
outline.gist: Being one can suggest loneliness or weakness, so the Quran pairs the One with the Supreme to show His oneness is unique dominance, free of any flaw.

outline.heading: Created in stages in three darknesses
outline.gist: The One who created and provides for you needs no intermediary; everyone can go straight to Allah.

outline.heading: Allah does not need our faith; each bears his own burden
outline.gist: Worship benefits us, not Him; everyone is judged on their own deeds and cannot excuse wrongdoing because others did it.

outline.heading: The fickle person versus the devout worshipper at night
outline.gist: One turns to Allah only in hardship and forgets Him in ease; the other prays through the night, fearing the hereafter and hoping for mercy.

outline.heading: Are those who know equal to those who do not
outline.gist: Islamic knowledge is not trivia; it is knowledge put into action that improves character across the board.

outline.heading: Those who do good will have good; Allah's earth is spacious
outline.gist: Consistent good brings its reward despite mistreatment, and a persecuted believer can move to where he can worship in peace.

outline.heading: Patience rewarded without limit
outline.gist: Unlike an act such as salah that ends, patience is a state, so its reward keeps accruing for as long as you remain in it.

outline.heading: Commanded to worship Allah with sincere devotion
outline.gist: The Prophet is told to declare the purpose of the deen; sincerity means the primary motive is Allah's pleasure, in private and in public.

outline.heading: The best message makes skins tremble
outline.gist: Allah links the rain and withering crops with the Quran; when the signs in the book and the signs in creation come together, the heart softens and trembles.

outline.heading: Parable of the slave with quarrelling masters
outline.gist: Allah compares a slave owned by several disputing masters with one owned by a single master.

outline.heading: Slavery in Islam compared with American slavery
outline.gist: A tangent: Islamic law restricted slavery and opened paths to freedom, so many leading scholars of the early generations were formerly enslaved people who led society.

outline.heading: One chain of command: devotion to one God
outline.gist: Serving many gods leaves you devoted to none; worshipping Allah alone brings the full benefit of spirituality.

outline.heading: You will die and disputes are settled before Allah
outline.gist: Differences between religions will not be definitively settled in this world but on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: The worst deeds forgiven, rewarded by the best
outline.gist: Allah wipes out the worst of what believers did and rewards all their deeds at the level of their best one; is Allah not sufficient for His servant.

outline.heading: You are not a keeper over them
outline.gist: Guidance benefits the one guided; the Prophet conveys and does not compel.

outline.heading: Souls taken in sleep: close to death every night
outline.gist: Allah takes souls in sleep and returns those whose time has not come; sleep as the sister of death should shake anyone who feels secure in disbelief.

outline.heading: Crediting blessings to one's own knowledge; provision is not favour
outline.gist: People cry out in hardship and then claim success came from their own skill; wealth given to disbelievers is no sign of Allah's pleasure.

outline.heading: Do not despair of Allah's mercy
outline.gist: One of the most powerful verses: Allah forgives all sins for those who have wronged themselves.

outline.heading: Repent before the punishment arrives
outline.gist: Tawbah is accepted until death is seen; procrastinating leaves people saying they wish Allah had guided them or given another chance.

outline.heading: Chance after chance was given
outline.gist: Every morning your soul was returned as a new chance, yet the arrogant rejected the signs; the mindful are delivered.

outline.heading: The trumpet, the shining earth and the witnesses
outline.gist: Two blasts end and restart life; the prophets testify they conveyed the message, shifting liability to those who received it.

outline.heading: Driven to hell in groups: no one goes without the message
outline.gist: Every inhabitant of the fire admits messengers came to them; those who never received the message will be tested on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Led to paradise; the final word is praise
outline.gist: The righteous enter forever and the last statement of the Day of Judgment is alhamdulillah.

outline.heading: Gates flung open versus gates already open
outline.gist: The extra waw in the paradise verse shows its gates are already open in welcome, like seeing and smelling the sea before you reach it.

outline.heading: Interlude
The seven Ha Meem surahs and their shared themes
outline.gist: All Makkan, all opening with Ha Meem, all praising the Quran and mentioning Musa: the torch of leadership passing to this ummah, unity, and gentleness with those who insult you.

outline.heading: Ghafir opens: forgiver of sin, accepter of repentance
outline.gist: The surah opens with names that join forgiveness and severity.

outline.heading: Dawah without power; do not be deceived by their prosperity
outline.gist: Giving dawah is hard when you are not in power; earlier nations disputed with falsehood to make the truth look shaky and were seized.

outline.heading: Angels as role models and their dua for believers
outline.gist: The bearers of the throne ask forgiveness for those who repent and pray for their parents, spouses and children to join them in paradise.

outline.heading: Call on Allah sincerely, even if it angers the disbelievers
outline.gist: Keep inviting with sincerity and wishing good for all; the haters can keep hating, but no one is forced.

outline.heading: To whom does the dominion belong this day
outline.gist: On that day sovereignty is the One, the Supreme; the negation of injustice is total.

outline.heading: Warn them of the approaching day
outline.gist: Every day brings us closer to death and the Judgment, when hearts rise to the throats and the wrongdoers have no friend or intercessor.

outline.heading: Musa sent to Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun
outline.gist: They call him a liar, order the sons of believers killed, and Pharaoh resolves to kill Musa as a security threat; Musa seeks refuge in Allah.

outline.heading: The believer of Pharaoh's household speaks up
outline.gist: An Egyptian hiding his faith asks if they would kill a man for saying his Lord is Allah while bringing proofs, and reminds those in power they cannot stop Allah's punishment.

outline.heading: He warns of the fate of earlier nations
outline.gist: Growing bolder, he fears for them the fate of the people of Nuh, Ad and Thamud and the Day they will flee.

outline.heading: Yusuf came to you before
outline.gist: Egypt honoured Yusuf but never accepted his message and was relieved when he died; that is how transgressors are left to stray.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's tower: a distraction with no answer
outline.gist: Having no reply, Pharaoh orders Haman to build a tower to look for Musa's God, though he knew Musa was truthful.

outline.heading: Follow me: this life is fleeting
outline.gist: He invites his people to the path of guidance, says reward is the same for men and women, and contrasts his call to salvation with their call to the fire.

outline.heading: Entrusting his affair to Allah; help from where you never expect
outline.gist: Now openly Muslim, he entrusts himself to Allah and is protected; the lesson is to live and convey Islam and expect allies from unexpected places.

outline.heading: Be patient, seek forgiveness, glorify Allah
outline.gist: Those who dispute without proof want dominance; when dawah is rejected, increase your remembrance to strengthen your connection.

outline.heading: Call upon Me and I will respond
outline.gist: Anyone searching for God, of any religion, should call on Him and see His response; that is the core of the true deen.

outline.heading: Signs in the earth, the sky and our form
outline.gist: Allah made the earth a settlement and the sky a canopy and shaped us, so call on Him with sincere devotion.

outline.heading: From dust to old age: the cycle of life
outline.gist: The rise and fade of our strength should show us Allah's perfect power, the temporariness of life and our own humility.

outline.heading: The disputers dragged in chains
outline.gist: Those who reject the scriptures are asked where their idols are and admit they invoked nothing real; the punishment is for arrogance.

outline.heading: Results are not your concern
outline.gist: Whether the Prophet saw the outcome or not, his job was patience and dawah; ours is to persist and leave results to Allah.

outline.heading: Faith after seeing the punishment is too late
outline.gist: Earlier nations were stronger and richer and proud of their worldly knowledge; belief declared once the torment arrived did not benefit them.

outline.heading: Fussilat: a book explained in clear Arabic
outline.gist: The surah opens by presenting the Quran as the main way of calling to Allah.

outline.heading: The heavens and earth submit willingly
outline.gist: The six days of creation are detailed in parts; everything stays within the bounds Allah set, and even people with agency cannot step outside them.

outline.heading: The warning of Ad and Thamud silences a Quraysh leader
outline.gist: When the Prophet recited the warning, a Quraysh leader put his hand on his mouth; he knew it was true but still did not accept Islam.

outline.heading: Ears, eyes and skin testify against them
outline.gist: On the Day of Judgment the enemies of Allah are confronted by their own bodies, made to speak by Allah.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone
themes.note: Sincere devotion to Allah alone with no intermediaries is the spine of Az-Zumar, argued from creation and the parable of the many masters.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Sincerity means the primary motive of worship is Allah's pleasure, in private and in public, with other benefits secondary.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Al-Wahid always comes with Al-Qahhar so that Allah's oneness is understood as supremacy, not loneliness.

themes.label: Patience (sabr) and perseverance
themes.note: Patience is a state rather than a single act, so its reward is without limit.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Never despair of mercy, but do not procrastinate: repentance closes when death or punishment is seen.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: Every night's sleep takes the soul, so we are close to death daily and each morning is a new chance.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The trumpet, the witnesses, and the groups led to hell and paradise; no one is punished without the message reaching them.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: Dawah from weakness, the believer of Pharaoh's household as a model, and focusing on the effort while leaving results to Allah.

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: Real knowledge is put into action and changes character, unlike trivia.

maxims: Intermediaries are a detour around the main problem
Patience is a state, so its reward never stops
Link the signs in the book with the signs outside it
Prosperity is not a sign of Allah's pleasure
Your job is the dawah; the results belong to Allah

stories.point: A man of power who hid his faith argued for Musa with logic and courage; help for the truth can come from unexpected places.
Egypt honoured Yusuf yet ignored his message and was relieved when he died, a warning against respecting a messenger while rejecting the message.
He stopped the Prophet's recitation in fear, knew it was the truth, and still refused it.

Contrast between slavery under Islamic law and North American chattel slavery
takeaways: Make the pleasure of Allah the primary motive of every act of worship, in private and in public
Do not delay tawbah; treat each morning as a returned soul and a new chance
Bear hardship and mistreatment with patience, knowing its reward has no limit
Keep conveying Islam through words and actions with sincerity and gentleness, and leave the results to Allah
When dawah is rejected, increase your dhikr and seek forgiveness rather than losing heart

4:48.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغۡفِرُ أَن يُشۡرَكَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَن يُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰٓ إِثۡمًا عَظِيمًا
4:48.en: Lo! Allah forgiveth not that a partner should be ascribed unto Him. He forgiveth (all) save that to whom He will. Whoso ascribeth partners to Allah, he hath indeed invented a tremendous sin

4:135.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَوِ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَۚ إِن يَكُنۡ غَنِيًّا أَوۡ فَقِيرࣰ ا فَٱللَّهُ أَوۡلَىٰ بِهِمَاۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعۡدِلُواْۚ وَإِن تَلۡوُۥٓاْ أَوۡ تُعۡرِضُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا
4:135.en: O ye who believe! Be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for Allah, even though it be against yourselves or (your) parents or (your) kindred, whether (the case be of) a rich man or a poor man, for Allah is nearer unto both (them ye are). So follow not passion lest ye lapse (from truth) and if ye lapse or fall away, then lo! Allah is ever Informed of what ye do

43:81.ar: قُلۡ إِن كَانَ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ وَلَدࣱ فَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلۡعَٰبِدِينَ
43:81.en: Say (O Muhammad): If the Beneficent One hath a son, then, I shall be first among the worshippers. (But there is no son)

Bip5d8MrOAU.speaker_note: fourth episode of his Muslim Wellness Network series; mentions his own clinical practice on the wards
Bip5d8MrOAU.title: The Philosophy of Islamic Thought #4: Ethical and Moral Philosophy of Islam
Bip5d8MrOAU.one_line: Islamic ethics as a theocentric, virtue-oriented, law-structured system that blends rules, character and consequences under an absolute commitment to righteousness.
Bip5d8MrOAU.summary: He argues that Islam starts its reform with morality because morality touches every part of life, unlike ideologies that begin from economics or the social contract. He defines Islamic ethics as theocentric, virtue-oriented and law-structured, grounded in revelation and rational accountability. Because Allah is the reference point, Muslim moral lines stay fixed while secular societies' lines drift, as with sexual ethics, and he links this to why shirk is unforgivable. Bringing Islam back means restoring its morals, not punishments. Islam is a hybrid of deontological, virtue and consequentialist ethics, shown through the organ-transplant dilemma, end-of-life care, the role of intention and the permitted exceptions to lying. Humans are morally responsible, rational agents with a fitrah and free will, and Sharia is a moral, legal and spiritual code. A moral code must cohere with a view of reality and of the good life, which atheistic frameworks cannot supply. He separates values, principles and ethical ranking, insisting justice outranks loyalty even against one's mother, and that righteousness carries infinite weight so ends never justify means. He closes by rejecting the split between private belief and public conduct and urges that youth learn cheating is wrong before fussing over details.

outline.heading: Opening
Islam begins its reform with morality
outline.gist: Capitalism, communism and liberalism start from one branch of life; morality touches everything, so Islam starts with the moral individual and society.

outline.heading: Epistemology first, then four disciplines
outline.gist: Every ideology must justify its knowledge; the series will cover morality, economics, wellbeing and governance.

outline.heading: The revival of Muslim philosophical writing
outline.gist: Such thinkers were once scarce and labelled deviant, a legacy of colonialism and Ottoman decline; the field is now maturing.

outline.heading: Definition: theocentric, virtue-oriented, law-structured
outline.gist: Revelation gives the principles like code, and reason applies them to every new situation; otherwise the Quran would need every scenario spelled out.

outline.heading: Theocentric: Allah as the reference point of good and evil
outline.gist: Secular morality follows society and drifts with war, media and culture; a Muslim dropped anywhere knows the same red lines.

outline.heading: Why shirk is unforgivable: a variable moral source
outline.gist: With more than one source of value the line in the sand keeps shifting; tawhid keeps morality constant.

outline.heading: Shifted lines in sexual ethics
outline.gist: Discussion itself has become impossible and identity is now tied to attraction; Islam cares about actions, not every desire needing fulfilment.

outline.heading: Bringing Islam back means bringing back its morals
outline.gist: Many imagine punishments and coercion; the real transformation the Companions found was ethical.

outline.heading: A sound moral code matters more than outward practice
outline.gist: He prefers someone weak in ritual with a solid moral ranking over someone praying while the moral code is broken.

outline.heading: Where good and evil come from
outline.gist: The sects differ on reason and revelation, a debate to enjoy not fight over; most moral codes worldwide trace back to revelation, and for Muslims the source is theocentric either way.

outline.heading: Three ethical schools and three questions
outline.gist: Rules, character and outcomes correspond to deontological, virtue and consequentialist ethics; Islam affirms inherent right and wrong.

outline.heading: Islam as a hybrid of all three
outline.gist: Islam accepts virtue ethics and a consequentialist awareness, but never pure utilitarianism, a mature system not yet named academically.

outline.heading: The transplant dilemma
outline.gist: Killing a dying patient to save five: rule and virtue ethics refuse, while utilitarian reasoning bends under need.

outline.heading: The Muslim answer and end-of-life care
outline.gist: A Muslim never hastens death; stopping treatment or relieving pain with a fatal side effect is not killing, because intention matters.

outline.heading: Intention and the violent pursuer
outline.gist: Courts already weigh intent; asked where a friend hides, rule ethics forbids lying while consequences point the other way.

outline.heading: Truthfulness and its exceptions
outline.gist: Compliments to a spouse, deceiving an enemy in war and reconciling people are not lying, but judging a contest is; lying to save the oppressed is allowed.

outline.heading: The human being: responsible, rational, fitrah, free will
outline.gist: Humans can go either way, reason ethically for themselves and carry an inner moral compass that abuse can corrupt.

outline.heading: Sharia as a moral, legal and spiritual code
outline.gist: Acts are judged by intention as well as outward conformity; moral psychology is embedded in law.

outline.heading: What is real: morality needs a coherent reality
outline.gist: Reality is created and sustained by a wise Creator; moral systems built on randomness collapse from incoherence.

outline.heading: Why be good if nothing follows?
outline.gist: Without accountability you cannot convince a poor person not to cheat; people want the moral code without the framework that makes it work.

outline.heading: The good life
outline.gist: Just conduct, cultivated virtue and conscious devotion leading to success in both lives; hedonism cannot explain altruism or moderation.

outline.heading: Values, principles and ethics
outline.gist: Values are what matter, principles are rules derived from them, ethics is the ranking used when values collide.

outline.heading: Your mother runs a red light: justice over loyalty
outline.gist: Truthful testimony is required even against parents; loyalty is a real virtue but never outranks justice.

outline.heading: The three core ethics and the infinite weight of righteousness
outline.gist: Righteousness generates justice and incorruptibility, and outweighs everything placed against it.

outline.heading: Pursuit of truth in belief and in people's rights
outline.gist: The Quran grounds worship in evidence, even saying the Prophet would worship a son if one existed; rights are sacred and never violated.

outline.heading: Ends never justify means: the straight path
outline.gist: Moral absolutism ignores outcomes; Muslims ask for a path, not a destination, and leave results to Allah.

outline.heading: Judge speakers by their ethics, not their fatwas
outline.gist: Fiqh choices are negotiable, but violating core ethics disqualifies a speaker; a mortgage fatwa does not.

outline.heading: No split between private belief and public conduct
outline.gist: Ethics runs continuously from prayer to contracts to governance; it is a way of life, not a department of it.

outline.heading: Teach youth that cheating is wrong first
outline.gist: Obsessing over halal details while cheating openly shows how far people are from the essence of the din.

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone

themes.note: Atheistic frameworks cannot justify the moral code they borrow.

Judge scholars and speakers by their ethics, not by fatwas you dislike
Live your din's ethics outside the masjid, starting with honesty and not cheating

36:68.ar: وَمَن نُّعَمِّرۡهُ نُنَكِّسۡهُ فِي ٱلۡخَلۡقِۚ أَفَلَا يَعۡقِلُونَ
36:68.en: He whom we bring unto old age, We reverse him in creation (making him go back to weakness after strength). Have ye then no sense

36:69.ar: وَمَا عَلَّمۡنَٰهُ ٱلشِّعۡرَ وَمَا يَنۢبَغِي لَهُۥٓۚ إِنۡ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكۡرࣱ وَقُرۡءَانࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
36:69.en: And We have not taught him (Muhammad) poetry, nor is it meet for him. This is naught else than a Reminder and a Lecture making plain

36:70.ar: لِّيُنذِرَ مَن كَانَ حَيࣰّ ا وَيَحِقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
36:70.en: To warn whosoever liveth, and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers

36:71.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّا خَلَقۡنَا لَهُم مِّمَّا عَمِلَتۡ أَيۡدِينَآ أَنۡعَٰمࣰ ا فَهُمۡ لَهَا مَٰلِكُونَ
36:71.en: Have they not seen how We have created for them of Our handiwork the cattle, so that they are their owners

36:72.ar: وَذَلَّلۡنَٰهَا لَهُمۡ فَمِنۡهَا رَكُوبُهُمۡ وَمِنۡهَا يَأۡكُلُونَ
36:72.en: And have subdued them unto them, so that some of them they have for riding, some for food

36:73.ar: وَلَهُمۡ فِيهَا مَنَٰفِعُ وَمَشَارِبُۚ أَفَلَا يَشۡكُرُونَ
36:73.en: Benefits and (divers) drinks have they from them. Will they not then give thanks

36:74.ar: وَٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ءَالِهَةࣰ لَّعَلَّهُمۡ يُنصَرُونَ
36:74.en: And they have taken (other) gods beside Allah, in order that they may be helped

36:75.ar: لَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ نَصۡرَهُمۡ وَهُمۡ لَهُمۡ جُندࣱ مُّحۡضَرُونَ
36:75.en: It is not in their power to help them; but they (the worshippers) are unto them a host in arms

36:76.ar: فَلَا يَحۡزُنكَ قَوۡلُهُمۡۘ إِنَّا نَعۡلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعۡلِنُونَ
36:76.en: So let not their speech grieve thee (O Muhammad). Lo! We know what they conceal and what proclaim

2:165.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا يُحِبُّونَهُمۡ كَحُبِّ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَشَدُّ حُبࣰّ ا لِّلَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِذۡ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ أَنَّ ٱلۡقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
2:165.en: Yet of mankind are some who take unto themselves (objects of worship which they set as) rivals to Allah, loving them with a love like (that which is the due) of Allah (only) - those who believe are stauncher in their love for Allah - Oh, that those who do evil had but known, (on the day) when they behold the doom, that power belongeth wholly to Allah, and that Allah is severe in punishment

SF5P_Yf9mjE.speaker: adnan
SF5P_Yf9mjE.speaker_note: continues his own Yasin series; speaks of growing up in Syria and his uncle's orchard
SF5P_Yf9mjE.title: Tafseer of Surat Yasin, Part 7 (68-76)
SF5P_Yf9mjE.one_line: Life is measured by quality, not length: purpose sets you free, gratitude is the first step, and 'do not grieve' means stay the course.
SF5P_Yf9mjE.summary: He begins from the surah's core claim that quality of life tracks how alive the heart is. The verse about reversing the creation of those given long life shows that life was never about quantity: we peak and decline, so live well rather than long. Without purpose a void remains however healthy your lifestyle, and a cause that will not save you before Allah is a wasted life. He asks what people actually get out of Islam, answering for himself: meaning and serenity in any circumstance. The companions died far from home leaving nothing because they were free, and someone who wants nothing from the powerful has no leverage on him; he illustrates with Bilal refusing to use his years with the Prophet to win his brother a bride. The Quran warns those who are alive, meaning living hearts, so we pray for others rather than judge them. Livestock subdued for us call for gratitude, the first step without which a heart is dead, though he adds a call for moderation in eating meat. Anything loved like Allah enslaves you. Finally, do not grieve over what they say was revealed amid persecution and means stay the course: the Prophet never saw the conquests, and we may not see the change we work for, but enough people of quality will get it done.

outline.heading: Quality of life tracks the life of the heart
outline.gist: Purpose, connection with Allah and living for something beyond yourself are what raise quality of life.

outline.heading: The believer of Yasin still lives
outline.gist: He lost his life young, yet his stand lives on with Allah and with us.

outline.heading: The finale, and a reading note
outline.gist: The closing verses solidify the surah's ideas; he notes how the verb in this verse is read.

outline.heading: Whoever We give long life, We reverse in creation
outline.gist: The longer you live, the more you return to how you began, dependent and frail.

outline.heading: Do not measure life by quantity
outline.gist: If length mattered we would keep improving with age; instead we peak in our thirties and decline.

outline.heading: Why he chose Yasin
outline.gist: He chose it for its theme of real life, not its fame; this is why Muslims follow the teachings.

outline.heading: Without meaning there is a void
outline.gist: A healthy lifestyle without faith leaves a hole; purpose helps anyone, but a cause that will not save you before Allah wastes your life.

outline.heading: Everyone sells himself to something
outline.gist: Each morning every person sells himself to some cause that either frees him or ruins him.

outline.heading: What do you get out of Islam?
outline.gist: His answer: meaning and serenity in any circumstance; if Islam is only hardship to you, you will not last seventy years.

outline.heading: Whatever hand you are dealt
outline.gist: Healthy or sick, rich or poor, the cause does not change, and you follow only the divine.

outline.heading: Companions who died far away leaving nothing
outline.gist: Abu Ayyub could have profited from owning the house where the Prophet stayed, yet asked to be carried as far as possible and buried there.

outline.heading: Wanting nothing makes you free
outline.gist: Needs give others leverage over you; someone who wants nothing they have is free and, to them, dangerous.

outline.heading: Islam spread because its carriers were free
outline.gist: The decades of expansion after the Prophet came from people who could have cashed in and did not.

outline.heading: Bilal asks a bride for his brother
outline.gist: Bilal refused to use their years with the Prophet as leverage; honest asking was enough and the family agreed.

outline.heading: Live well, not long
outline.gist: If a long life is written for you, so be it; either way, live well in the time you get.

outline.heading: Not poetry, but a reminder and clear Quran
outline.gist: The Prophet was not taught poetry; what he brought is a reminder and a recited book.

outline.heading: To warn whoever is alive
outline.gist: The Prophet was not going to preach to graves; alive here means a living heart, linking back to verse 11.

outline.heading: Pray for hearts rather than judge them
outline.gist: We make dua that Allah kindles life in others' hearts; otherwise the decree falls on those who refuse.

outline.heading: Have they not seen what We made for them
outline.gist: He recites the passage on livestock created for people.

outline.heading: What our hands made, not theirs
outline.gist: This supports his reading of verse 35: people use laws that already exist but make nothing themselves.

outline.heading: Powerful animals made tame
outline.gist: Camels, horses and bulls are far stronger than us yet Allah made them submissive to us.

outline.heading: Rides, food and every use: livestock as complete blessing
outline.gist: An'am stands for holistic blessing: transport, food, milk, labour, wool and hides.

outline.heading: Eating meat in moderation
outline.gist: Our heavy meat and dairy diets damage the planet; he grew up eating mostly legumes, and Muslims should discuss restraint.

outline.heading: Will they not be grateful? Gratitude as the first step
outline.gist: Without gratitude the heart is dead; we cannot tolerate ingratitude in our children, yet Allah gives us far more.

outline.heading: Gods besides Allah enslave you
outline.gist: Anything loved or feared like Allah, even desire, counts; whatever you value most, you become its soldier.

outline.heading: Do not grieve: revealed amid persecution
outline.gist: Revealed when Quraysh threatened to kill the Prophet, as the township threatened its messengers; Allah knows what they hide and show.

outline.heading: Stay the course
outline.gist: You will not succeed at first or see the fruit soon; the Prophet died with Islam still a small circle.

outline.heading: You may not live to see the change
outline.gist: The Prophet never saw the conquests; we hope for a free Palestine, Muslim unity and a saved planet, and must keep working anyway.

outline.heading: The first command in the juz
outline.gist: Through this juz there is no direct command until this one: do not be bothered by what they say.

outline.heading: A promise, and enough people of quality
outline.gist: If enough people stay the course it will work out; it needs quality, not mass numbers.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Life is measured by quality, not length; everyone sells himself to some cause, so choose one that saves you.

themes.label: Freedom, rights and responsibility
themes.note: Wanting nothing others hold removes their leverage; the companions were free.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: Abu Ayyub and Bilal as people who would not cash in on their nearness to the Prophet.

themes.label: Guidance (hidayah)
themes.note: The Quran benefits living hearts; pray for others rather than judge them.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Livestock as complete blessing; gratitude is the first step without which the heart is dead.

themes.label: Moderation and balance (wasatiyyah)
themes.note: Eat meat with restraint for the planet's sake.

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone
themes.note: Anything loved like Allah, including desire, becomes a master.

themes.label: Patience (sabr) and perseverance
themes.note: Do not grieve means stay the course even if you never see the results.

quran.point: Those who love others as they should love Allah: anything given Allah's place is a rival.

hadith.gist: Every person goes out in the morning and sells himself, either freeing himself or ruining himself.

maxims: Live well, not long
Don't measure life with quantity
If I have something you want, you're not free
Whatever you value highly, you are enslaved to
Just stay the course
Enough people with quality to get it done

stories.point: He gave up the comfort of the Prophet's house to die at the farthest point of the campaign.
Ask honestly; never use blessings such as companionship as leverage.
Huge, frightening animals are made tame for us, a blessing to be grateful for.

stories.who: The Prophet under threat in Mecca and the boycott
stories.point: He was told not to grieve and to stay the course though he never saw the results.

contemporary: Retirement savings planning
Meat and dairy consumption and climate damage
Hope for a free Palestine and Muslim unity
takeaways: Judge your life by its purpose and quality, not by how long it lasts.
Want nothing from people so that no one has leverage over you.
Make gratitude the first step of reviving the heart.
Eat meat in moderation.
Keep working for change you may never live to see.

36:77.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ أَنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰهُ مِن نُّطۡفَةࣲ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
36:77.en: Hath not man seen that We have created him from a drop of seed? Yet lo! he is an open opponent

36:78.ar: وَضَرَبَ لَنَا مَثَلࣰ ا وَنَسِيَ خَلۡقَهُۥۖ قَالَ مَن يُحۡيِ ٱلۡعِظَٰمَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمࣱ‏
36:78.en: And he hath coined for Us a similitude, and hath forgotten the fact of his creation, saying: Who will revive these bones when they have rotted away

36:79.ar: قُلۡ يُحۡيِيهَا ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنشَأَهَآ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ خَلۡقٍ عَلِيمٌ
36:79.en: Say: He will revive them Who produced them at the first, for He is Knower of every creation

36:80.ar: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّجَرِ ٱلۡأَخۡضَرِ نَارࣰ ا فَإِذَآ أَنتُم مِّنۡهُ تُوقِدُونَ
36:80.en: Who hath appointed for you fire from the green tree, and behold! ye kindle from it

36:81.ar: أَوَلَيۡسَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَخۡلُقَ مِثۡلَهُمۚ بَلَىٰ وَهُوَ ٱلۡخَلَّٰقُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
36:81.en: Is not He Who created the heavens and the earth Able to create the like of them? Aye, that He is! for He is the All-Wise Creator

36:82.ar: إِنَّمَآ أَمۡرُهُۥٓ إِذَآ أَرَادَ شَيۡـًٔا أَن يَقُولَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
36:82.en: But His command, when He intendeth a thing, is only that He saith unto it: Be! and it is

36:83.ar: فَسُبۡحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِۦ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
36:83.en: Therefor Glory be to Him in Whose hand is the dominion over all things! Unto Him ye will be brought back

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And when Abraham said (unto his Lord): My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead, He said: Dost thou not believe? Abraham said: Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease. (His Lord) said: Take four of the birds and cause them to incline unto thee, then place a part of them on each hill, then call them, they will come to thee in haste, and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise

75:3.en: Thinketh man that We shall not assemble his bones

75:4.ar: بَلَىٰ قَٰدِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُۥ
75:4.en: Yea, verily. We are Able to restore his very fingers

7:54.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ يُغۡشِي ٱلَّيۡلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ يَطۡلُبُهُۥ حَثِيثࣰ ا وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ وَٱلنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّرَٰتِۭ بِأَمۡرِهِۦٓۗ أَلَا لَهُ ٱلۡخَلۡقُ وَٱلۡأَمۡرُۗ تَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
7:54.en: Lo! your Lord is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days, then mounted He the Throne. He covereth the night with the day, which is in haste to follow it, and hath made the sun and the moon and the stars subservient by His command. His verily is all creation and commandment. Blessed be Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

2:37.ar: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتࣲ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:37.en: Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him. Lo! He is the relenting, the Merciful

9:118.ar: وَعَلَى ٱلثَّلَٰثَةِ ٱلَّذِينَ خُلِّفُواْ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا ضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتۡ وَضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَنفُسُهُمۡ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَن لَّا مَلۡجَأَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّآ إِلَيۡهِ ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ لِيَتُوبُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
9:118.en: And to the three also (did He turn in mercy) who were left behind, when the earth, vast as it is, was straitened for them, and their own souls were straitened for them till they bethought them that there is no refuge from Allah save toward Him. Then turned He unto them in mercy that they (too) might turn (repentant unto Him). Lo! Allah! He is the Relenting, the Merciful

8gnkTXLWsUQ.speaker: adnan
8gnkTXLWsUQ.speaker_note: concludes his own Yasin series in the first person
8gnkTXLWsUQ.title: Tafseer of Surat Yasin, Part 8 (77-83)
8gnkTXLWsUQ.one_line: Concluding Yasin: the one who gave life the first time will give it again, so stop arguing about resurrection and live the life you have.
8gnkTXLWsUQ.summary: He closes the surah on its theme of life and resurrection. People have always struggled with life's origin and end because they cannot control either. The human being came from a drop to become an articulate opponent without contributing anything, yet he coins examples for Allah, like the Qurayshi chief who crumbled a decayed bone and mocked the idea of revival. Our problem with Allah, he says, is the granting of life, and Allah's problem with us is the same: I gave you life, so live it before arguing about the second one. The answer is that the One who made it the first time will do it again; He knows every creature and can restore even fingertips. Fire from the green tree shows a cycle of life turning to death and back that runs through all creation, and graves opened after a decade show how fully we return to the earth, all of it recorded. The Creator of the heavens can easily create the like of us; His command 'be' does not mean instant, as the universe took six of His days. There is no running from Allah, only back to Him, as Adam and the three who stayed behind learned. He ends urging people to make life a vehicle for truth like the believer of the township, warning that inherited, habitual Islam is less alive than even Abu Jahl's passion for a wrong cause.

outline.heading: The age-old struggle with life and its end
outline.gist: Since humans first contemplated mortality they have asked where life comes from, why it ends and whether it returns.

outline.heading: We cannot control life or death
outline.gist: Humans hate not being in control, yet cannot control aging or when they die.

outline.heading: A life worth living is about quality
outline.gist: A short glimmer of real light is better than a long darkness; he then recites the closing verses.

outline.heading: From a drop to an open opponent
outline.gist: From a single microscopic cell against overwhelming odds, the human becomes a creature who argues articulately, with no contribution of his own.

outline.heading: Self-evident truths that repeat every time
outline.gist: The process happens again and again; where do the intelligence, ego and willpower come from?

outline.heading: He coins examples for Us and forgets his own creation
outline.gist: The human presumes to share his wisdom with the divine while forgetting where he came from.

outline.heading: The chief who killed the first unnamed believers
outline.gist: A Qurayshi chief who had killed early Muslims, enslaved converts whose names are barely recorded, came to the Prophet with a decaying bone.

outline.heading: Who will revive bones that have decayed?
outline.gist: Crumbling the bone and laughing, he mocked resurrection; the Prophet answered that Allah would raise him.

outline.heading: Our mental block about the granting of life
outline.gist: We have this life without contributing to it, yet call a second one impossible.

outline.heading: Ibrahim asks how Allah gives life
outline.gist: Ibrahim believed but wanted to understand, and was shown the birds come back together; Allah's ways are beyond comprehension.

outline.heading: Live the life I gave you first
outline.gist: Allah's problem with us mirrors ours with Him: He gave us life and we waste it, arguing about the second round.

outline.heading: The body was given so you may find the spirit
outline.gist: Allah made the heart pump; your job is to enlighten it. The One who made it the first time will do it again.

outline.heading: He knows every creation
outline.gist: From single cells to the most complex creature, nothing that ever drew one breath is missed.

outline.heading: Gathering the bones down to the fingertips
outline.gist: Allah can restore a person to the detail of his fingerprint.

outline.heading: Fire from the green tree
outline.gist: A tree full of water becomes fuel for fire; Allah creates the paradoxes of water and fire, life and death.

outline.heading: The endless cycle of life and death
outline.gist: The tree burns, enriches the earth and grows again; everything follows this cycle, yet people exempt themselves.

outline.heading: Resurrection as the Meccans' main objection
outline.gist: Besides intercessors, their chief denial was being raised again, which was the heart of the Prophet's message.

outline.heading: Graves found empty after a decade
outline.gist: Reopened graves after ten years hold nothing; the body returns to the earth, and every particle is recorded.

outline.heading: The Creator of the heavens can create their like
outline.gist: We are tiny compared with the cosmos; bringing us back costs Him nothing.

outline.heading: Al-Khallaq al-Alim
outline.gist: The intensive form means One who creates abundantly over long periods and knows everything about what He creates.

outline.heading: Be, and it is
outline.gist: No labs or teams are involved; your being here should make your return an easy conclusion.

outline.heading: Worry about being asked how you lived
outline.gist: Instead of questioning the second life, prepare to show what you did with this one.

outline.heading: Be does not mean instant
outline.gist: The universe took six of His days, periods we now know span billions of years; we are made of time and expect God to act on our timeline.

outline.heading: In His hand is the dominion of everything
outline.gist: Exalt Him and do not get too worked up by what you see in the world; all returns to Him.

outline.heading: Adam running in paradise
outline.gist: After eating from the tree Adam ran out of shame, and Allah taught him the words to say instead.

oDIKpc3GaT8.speaker: adnan
oDIKpc3GaT8.speaker_note: leads the night prayer and continues his own series on the movements of salah from earlier nights
oDIKpc3GaT8.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 24: Fourth Night of Tahajjud
oDIKpc3GaT8.one_line: Reminders on the meaning of ruku and rising: bowing to Allah alone, exalting Him, and Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b's request for Paradise.
oDIKpc3GaT8.summary: Between the rakaat of this tahajjud night the sheikh continues his walk through the movements of prayer, explaining what each one means so that salah never turns into boredom or distraction. He recalls the standing, where the worshipper recites Allah's message back to Him and shows its value by memorizing it, taking the Prophet's slow, responsive night recitation as the model. He then turns to ruku. Bowing physically declares a difference of rank, which is why kings demand it, yet no human, however powerful, stands above you in that way, so you bow to Allah alone. The words of ruku put that rank into speech: subhan is an exaltation whose verb is left unsaid, and it reflects how you see Allah, flawless, His choices right, His decree acceptable to you. In the second reminder he argues that the first three movements belong to Allah, and the more one gives in them the more one can ask in the prostrations that follow; a long sujud means little after a rushed standing and ruku. He closes with Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b, who waited at the Prophet's door to serve him, heard him praising Allah through the night, and asked only for his company in Paradise, and was told to help with much prostration.

outline.heading: Interlude
The standing: reciting His message back to Him
outline.gist: Recalling the first movement: in qiyam you return Allah's message to Him by reciting it, and you show how much you value it by memorizing it word for word; the longer the standing, the better.

outline.heading: The Prophet's long night recitation
outline.gist: Ibn Mas'ud's night with the Prophet, who stood so long that he thought of leaving the prayer; the Prophet recited slowly, asking for Paradise and seeking refuge from the Fire as he passed those verses.

outline.heading: Ruku: magnify your Lord in it
outline.gist: Take whatever you can from the Prophet's standing, then move to ruku, which the Prophet said is the place to magnify the Lord.

outline.heading: Bowing only to the One above you
outline.gist: Kings demand a bow because it declares the subject's inferiority, but every human is your equal however much power or army they hold, so the bow belongs to Allah alone, the only One truly above you.

outline.heading: The words of ruku: how you see Allah
outline.gist: The adhkar of ruku exalt Him, and exaltation is your opinion of God: He is flawless, His choices are right, His decree is acceptable to you, and saying subhana rabbiyal-azim trains that view for the rest of life.

outline.heading: Interlude
Knowing the purpose of each movement
outline.gist: When you understand what each movement is for, prayer stops being boring or distracted because you know what you are doing in it.

outline.heading: Subhan: an exaltation with its verb unsaid
outline.gist: The bow sets the difference of status and the words confirm it; subhan is a verbal noun whose verb is dropped but understood, an exaltation so great it expresses how you view and understand Allah.

outline.heading: The first three movements belong to Him
outline.gist: Standing, ruku and rising are for Allah; the more you give in them, the more you can ask in the second three, and a long sujud means little without a long standing and ruku before it.

outline.heading: Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b's night at the Prophet's door
outline.gist: A teenage Rabi'ah waits at the Prophet's door to serve him, falls asleep and wakes repeatedly to hear him reciting, glorifying in ruku and praising Allah at length after rising.

outline.heading: Rabi'ah's request: company in Paradise
outline.gist: Offered anything, Rabi'ah refuses to ask for the world and asks for the Prophet's company in Paradise, and is told to help him achieve it through much prostration.

outline.heading: Interlude
