themes.note: Friendships that survive judgment are those built on righteousness; the people of the fire beg for an end.

maxims: Push back, but in the best way
With patience your enemies become your friends
Disunity came from envy, not from interpretation
Children are not assets that increase your net worth
Turn the page and say peace
Wealth is not a sign of Allah's pleasure

stories.point: Pharaoh mocked Musa's lack of gold and broke every promise once relief came, the same pattern Quraysh followed.
Allah turned the sea into the means of Pharaoh's end, a promise that the Prophet would likewise be helped.

stories.who: Ibrahim's declaration to his father and people
stories.point: His descendants in Makkah kept his words but abandoned his tawhid, deceived by their prosperity.

contemporary: The COVID-19 pandemic as a sign of how Allah can bring the world to a standstill
Materialism in modern society
Disunity among Muslims today
The Rosetta Stone and Egyptian beliefs about the death of a pharaoh
takeaways: Keep inviting people to Allah even when insulted, and never stoop to the attacker's level
Defend your dignity truthfully and without vengeance, and aim to turn opponents into friends
Guard community unity and do not let envy or rivalry split believers
Run community affairs through genuine consultation where every voice is heard
Do not read wealth as divine approval, and treasure daughters and sons alike

16:90.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُ بِٱلۡعَدۡلِ وَٱلۡإِحۡسَٰنِ وَإِيتَآيِٕ ذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَيَنۡهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَٱلۡبَغۡيِۚ يَعِظُكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ
16:90.en: Lo! Allah enjoineth justice and kindness, and giving to kinsfolk, and forbiddeth lewdness and abomination and wickedness. He exhorteth you in order that ye may take heed

2:195.ar: وَأَنفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تُلۡقُواْ بِأَيۡدِيكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلتَّهۡلُكَةِ وَأَحۡسِنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
2:195.en: Spend your wealth for the cause of Allah, and be not cast by your own hands to ruin; and do good. Lo! Allah loveth the beneficent

16:97.ar: مَنۡ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنࣱ فَلَنُحۡيِيَنَّهُۥ حَيَوٰةࣰ طَيِّبَةࣰۖ وَلَنَجۡزِيَنَّهُمۡ أَجۡرَهُم بِأَحۡسَنِ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
16:97.en: Whosoever doeth right, whether male or female, and is a believer, him verily we shall quicken with good life, and We shall pay them a recompense in proportion to the best of what they used to do

17:34.ar: وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ مَالَ ٱلۡيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ أَشُدَّهُۥۚ وَأَوۡفُواْ بِٱلۡعَهۡدِۖ إِنَّ ٱلۡعَهۡدَ كَانَ مَسۡـُٔولࣰ ا
17:34.en: Come not near the wealth of the orphan save with that which is better till he come to strength; and keep the covenant. Lo! of the covenant it will be asked

17:23.ar: ۞وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۚ إِمَّا يَبۡلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلۡكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوۡ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفࣲّ وَلَا تَنۡهَرۡهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوۡلࣰ ا كَرِيمࣰ ا
17:23.en: Thy Lord hath decreed, that ye worship none save Him, and (that ye show) kindness to parents. If one of them or both of them attain old age with thee, say not "Fie" unto them nor repulse them, but speak unto them a gracious word

31:15.ar: وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشۡرِكَ بِي مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ فَلَا تُطِعۡهُمَاۖ وَصَاحِبۡهُمَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا مَعۡرُوفࣰ اۖ وَٱتَّبِعۡ سَبِيلَ مَنۡ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّۚ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
31:15.en: But if they strive with thee to make thee ascribe unto Me as partner that of which thou hast no knowledge, then obey them not. Consort with them in the world kindly, and follow the path of him who repenteth unto Me. Then unto Me will be your return, and I shall tell you what ye used to do

2:177.ar: ۞لَّيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ قِبَلَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَءَاتَى ٱلۡمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ ذَوِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱبۡنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَٱلسَّآئِلِينَ وَفِي ٱلرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُوفُونَ بِعَهۡدِهِمۡ إِذَا عَٰهَدُواْۖ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ فِي ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَحِينَ ٱلۡبَأۡسِۗ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُتَّقُونَ
2:177.en: It is not righteousness that ye turn your faces to the East and the West; but righteous is he who believeth in Allah and the Last Day and the angels and the Scripture and the prophets; and giveth wealth, for love of Him, to kinsfolk and to orphans and the needy and the wayfarer and to those who ask, and to set slaves free; and observeth proper worship and payeth the poor-due. And those who keep their treaty when they make one, and the patient in tribulation and adversity and time of stress. Such are they who are sincere. Such are the Allah-fearing

fOvsoUl0ixw.speaker: adnan
fOvsoUl0ixw.speaker_note: continues his own values series and tells his own story of learning public speaking
fOvsoUl0ixw.title: The Values of Islam: Excellence and Loyalty (Ihsan and Wafa')
fOvsoUl0ixw.one_line: Ihsan means investing your heart, not your ego, in everything you do; loyalty means never forgetting those who did you good. Both need justice to govern them.
fOvsoUl0ixw.summary: He pairs ihsan, excellence or virtuosity, with wafa', loyalty and fulfilling covenants, and from them derives birr. Both must be governed by justice, since one can excel at tyranny or be loyal to wrongdoing, which is why the Quran pairs ihsan with justice. Ihsan means filling every value to the top and always trying one's best, which takes courage because mediocrity shields people from criticism. The key is investing your heart rather than your ego in your work: then feedback is welcome because the goal is the work, not one's image. Excellence is about effort, not outcome; it puts one on a trajectory of improvement, and must be consistent across every role. The Jibril hadith shows ihsan as the pillar that drives inner perfection of worship. He shares how two teachers told him to stick to writing rather than speaking. Loyalty ran through the Prophet's life: his mother's journey to Madinah, Abu Talib, his devotion to Khadijah, honouring his foster mother at Hunayn and repaying every favour, leaving Abu Bakr's to Allah. Kindness to parents is the highest loyalty, bounded only by not obeying them in disobedience. Without these values no one can trust you, and the masjid must teach how ethics rank.

outline.heading: Opening
Excellence and loyalty need justice to govern them
outline.gist: One can excel at being a dictator or be loyal to wrong, so both must be governed by righteousness, justice and moral absolutes.

outline.heading: Ihsan prescribed in everything
outline.gist: The Quran pairs ihsan with justice, and the Prophet commanded excellence even in slaughtering an animal.

outline.heading: Being your best and trying your best
outline.gist: Ihsan fills every value to the top and opposes mediocrity, which is the easy way out.

outline.heading: Mediocrity is a choice to avoid vulnerability
outline.gist: Trying your best exposes you to hearing that your best is only all right, so people hold back.

outline.heading: Invest your heart, not your ego
outline.gist: When the heart is invested, feedback is welcome because the goal is the work; when the ego is invested, every criticism feels personal.

outline.heading: Ihsan in the hadith of Jibril
outline.gist: Worshipping Allah as if you see Him is the third pillar, perfecting worship until only seeing Him remains.

outline.heading: Excellence is about effort, not perfection
outline.gist: Ihsan extends to the inner life; we cannot be perfect but can be excellent, and steady effort with feedback keeps improving us.

outline.heading: Accepting that you are average
outline.gist: Few are naturally gifted; most must work for years, and admitting you are not that great is freeing and does not touch your worth.

outline.heading: Excellence must be consistent across roles
outline.gist: Trying hard only at a favourite game is a preference; ihsan means being the best parent, spouse, friend and student.

outline.heading: Perfecting acts of worship
outline.gist: We repeat prayers to perfect the craft; one excellent prayer outweighs countless mediocre ones, and Allah rewards by the best of deeds.

outline.heading: His own path in public speaking
outline.gist: Two teachers advised him to stick to writing; he kept trying, took feedback and improved by putting the work ahead of his ego.

outline.heading: The Prophet poured his heart into his work
outline.gist: With no ego in his work, he welcomed better ideas; loyalty means fulfilling one's word and covenants.

outline.heading: Loyalty in the Prophet's upbringing and marriage
outline.gist: His mother travelled to Madinah to connect him with his late father's relatives, Abu Talib kept his word, and he stayed loyal to Khadijah long after her death.

outline.heading: Kindness to parents as loyalty
outline.gist: Those who cared for you when you were most vulnerable deserve your best; ignoring them destroys any claim to ethics.

outline.heading: Be their best companion, but do not obey in sin
outline.gist: Even parents who push toward shirk are to be accompanied kindly; loyalty is ranked below righteousness.

outline.heading: The Prophet and his foster mother at Hunayn
outline.gist: He stopped distributing spoils to seat her on his cloak and paid from his own share to free her son and send her home provisioned.

outline.heading: Welcoming those you owe
outline.gist: Busy people avoid those they owe, but the Prophet was glad to repay anyone who had cared for him.

outline.heading: Repaying every favour, and Abu Bakr
outline.gist: In his final sermon he said he had repaid every kindness except Abu Bakr's, which he left to Allah.

outline.heading: Why these values come last: ranking ethics
outline.gist: Loyalty can be corrupted into helping wrongdoing, so ethics must be ranked and the masjid must teach that ranking.

outline.heading: Outro
